analyst_view.overall: Frosinone (7th, 20 points) host Parma (17th, 8 points) after both lost 5-1 last weekend, Frosinone at Milan and Parma at home to Roma; Frosinone also lost to Cagliari before that and want a reaction at the Stirpe. Frosinone have no fit senior centre-forward: Raimondo is out until about January and Birligea has a hamstring tear, so 13-million signing Bobcek, back from summer knee surgery, is set for his first start in Alvini's 4-2-3-1, with Bracaglia back from his ban at left-back; the numbers already take both strikers off Frosinone's goals (about -23%). Parma, under Alberto Gilardino and fighting relegation, keep their 3-5-2 with Elphege and probably Toure up front; Romero (counted, -13%), Drobnic and Diego Carlos still trained apart this week, and only Diego Carlos is missing from the numbers' list, while Ndiaye is back from his ban and Troilo is one booking from a ban. Referee Kevin Bonacina (3.2 cards a game) is now in the numbers. My only move is a small trim on shots and shots on target, which the striker absences don't reach.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals (1.5 Frosinone, 1.0 Parma); they take Raimondo and Birligea off Frosinone and Romero off Parma, and add both teams' leaky recent defending (Frosinone conceded 13 in six, Parma 12). Parma's back three is thinner than the numbers know without Diego Carlos, but Frosinone rely on Bobcek starting for the first time after knee surgery, so the two pull against each other and I stay at about 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.5 corners, 7.5 of them Frosinone's, and already add +16% for Frosinone's 53 corners in their last six games. Alvini's 4-2-3-1 with Ghedjemis and Kvernadze wide against a Parma side that sits in a 3-5-2 is the pattern the numbers already expect, so I stay at about 11.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.0 cards: they already take about 11% off for referee Kevin Bonacina's low count (3.2 a game) and some more because both teams have been booked less than usual lately. Parma are in a relegation fight with Ndiaye back from a red-card ban and Troilo one booking from a suspension, but nothing points to a heated game, so I stay at about 3.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 38.2 shots, a very high figure built on +34% for Frosinone's 135 shots in their last six games. The striker absences are only taken off goals: Frosinone play without Raimondo and Birligea and Bobcek is just back from surgery, and Parma lack Romero, so I trim mildly to about 36.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.1 shots on target and already add +20% for Frosinone's recent accuracy. Without their two main centre-forwards Frosinone should test the goalkeeper a little less, and Parma's attack without Romero is weak; a Parma defence without Diego Carlos limits the trim, so I go to about 10.8.
